clinical_knowledge.topic: Lower-Extremity Amputation Prosthetic Rehabilitation evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of lower-extremity amputation rehabilitation is essential for guiding safe prosthetic fitting and functional recovery.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic protocol for Amputation Lower Extremity Prosthetic Fitting, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: stump shaping, phantom limb neuropathic pain management, and gait training in diabetic transtibial below-knee amputee

Key HPI features: 58M diabetic 8 weeks post-transtibial amputation undergoing PM&R prosthetic fitting focusing on shrinker sock residual limb shaping, desensitization, neuropathic phantom pain titration with Pregabalin, and progressive parallel-bar prosthetic gait training.
Objective/Exam findings: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination required. Diagnostic workup tailored for Amputation Lower Extremity Prosthetic Fitting.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that phantom limb pain and residual-limb pain have the same cause.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Proceeding with prosthetic progression before confirming residual-limb skin integrity and volume stability.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Residual-limb infection, ischemia, or wound breakdown.

Refer to specialty team and provide comprehensive patient counseling
Assess clinical stability, monitor vital parameters, and perform targeted diagnostic investigations.
Implement targeted therapeutic interventions per evidence-based clinical practice guidelines.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

teaching.one_liner: Rehabilitation after transtibial amputation focused on residual-limb health, phantom pain management, prosthetic fitting, and safe gait recovery.
differentials: Peripheral arterial disease causing residual-limb ischemia
red_flags: Residual-limb redness, drainage, fever, or wound breakdown
New ischemic pain, discoloration, or rapidly progressive weakness

must_ask.say: Have you noticed any redness, drainage, skin breakdown, or worsening pain in your residual limb?
Do you feel painful sensations in the missing foot or leg, and what do they feel like?
Is your residual limb changing in size or making the socket feel loose or too tight?
Does wearing the prosthesis cause pressure areas, blisters, or pain?
What help do you need for transfers or walking, and have you had any falls?
